sections.label: The opening
sections.line: An open licence turned a CSV into a graph
sections.para: Jan van Dijke's AI Baseline Control Framework, published 2 October 2026, offers twenty controls for organisations deploying AI, mapped to the NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001 and the EU AI Act under CC BY-SA 4.0. Its only export was a CSV, and the licence allowed it to become a published graph vault the same day.

sections.label: Part one: the framework
sections.line: Twenty practical controls, including Access controls nobody else has
sections.para: AI BCF is written for deployers: twenty one-sentence controls in five categories, typed Baseline, Tier II or Trigger, each with why and how, citing fifty-four clauses. Its four Access controls have no equivalent in NIST, ISO or the AI Act. CC BY-SA 4.0 lets anyone build and share tools on it without asking.

sections.label: Part two: what we did with it
sections.line: The graph exposed links and gaps the CSV hides
sections.para: One script turned the CSV into a 127-node, 239-edge graph with an ontology, SKOS, JSON-LD, Turtle, eighty documents and a browser database, joined to the Regulation Graph. It found the four uncited Access controls, AI Act paths linking CM.1 to CM.4, four articles amended by 2026/1744, and shared clauses, with sgit.ai's overlay kept apart.
